open_points.subject: Disclosure-class order
open_points.text: “the members and the order have that one home” in `models`; but `canonical_values` “Owns ... The order of disclosure classes and the highest class of a set”
open_points.question: Does `models` own the disclosure-class ordering while `canonical_values` only owns the comparison/highest operation, or does `canonical_values` also own the ordering data?
options: `models` owns the ordered enumeration; `canonical_values` consumes it
`canonical_values` owns the ordering and `models` only declares the members
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the ordered enumeration, and `canonical_values` owns only the highest-class computation.

open_points.subject: Equal content submissions under A01 rule 4
open_points.text: `canonical_values` “Owns A01 rules 1 and 4” although it “Must not own Where a value is stored”; A01 rule 4 requires returning an existing stored record unchanged and preserving current-version and first-author facts.
open_points.question: Which module owns the stored-record behavior for an equal contract, implementation, trial case, flow version or value submission?
options: Each aggregate owner (`functions` or `flows`) enforces it using `store` uniqueness
`canonical_values` owns only equality/identity, with the stored behavior explicitly reassigned elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: `canonical_values` owns identity only; each aggregate module owns the equal-submission behavior and uses `store` to enforce uniqueness.

open_points.subject: Random identities for entity records
open_points.text: A01 rule 2 says `trial_execution_id`, `binding_id`, `run_id`, `approval_id` and `grant_id` “are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again,” but no State 3 module owns random identifier generation and collision retry.
open_points.question: Which module owns random-ID generation and the atomic check-and-remint behavior shared by `functions`, `bindings`, `runs` and `effects`?
options: Each record-owning module mints and retries through `store`
A separate lower-level identity source owns minting
open_points.default_guess: `store` atomically mints or collision-checks identifiers for the record-owning modules.

open_points.subject: Captured trial-case validation before file copying
open_points.text: “`runs` copies a spooled file into the content-addressed area only after every check ... `functions.add_captured_trial_case` would make,” but it “then calls `functions.add_captured_trial_case`, which checks ... the case's fit to it and adds it to the corpus.”
open_points.question: How can `runs` complete the `functions`-owned fit and size checks before copying files without duplicating those rules or invoking the mutating add operation too early?
options: `functions` exposes a non-mutating capture preflight capability
`functions` owns both copying and adding after `runs` supplies the eligible execution
`store` stages the copy and case write atomically under validation supplied by `functions`
open_points.default_guess: Add a non-mutating `functions` preflight capability, then let `runs` copy and call the final add operation.

open_points.subject: Uniqueness of configured agent names
open_points.text: M27 says agent “names are unique in an installation, and a configuration repeating one is refused at start,” while `installation` lists its start checks as file validity, token length and pairwise-distinct tokens without assigning the agent-name check.
open_points.question: Which module validates unique agent names and refuses startup when a name is repeated?
options: `installation` validates names while loading the protected configuration
`surface` validates names when constructing the actor/token lookup
